subject: Cognitive Science
title: Nudge Theory
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Nudge Theory.

hook.text: Countries that make organ donation opt-out instead of opt-in see donation rates jump from 15% to over 90%.

buildup.text: Thaler and Sunstein call this a 'nudge': redesigning the choice environment without removing any options.

discovery.text: Defaults are enormously powerful because people tend to stick with whatever is pre-selected.

twist.text: Nudges are controversial. Critics call it paternalism—manipulating choices while pretending people are free.

climax.text: The UK created a 'Nudge Unit' inside government. Its interventions have saved billions in tax collection alone.

punchline.text: Change the default, change the decision.

quiz.question: What is a 'nudge' in decision science?
options: Redesigning choice environments without removing options
